name: Vampiric Undead
background:
The Vampiric Undead are legions of monsters and their mortal servants led by powerful vampire Lords. These lords use their dark magic to raise the dead, and lead them to battle alongside their mortal servants. 

The Vampire Lords are members of the nobility from the western steppes who embraced necromancy after they were abandoned by the Empire during the Havoc Wars. Once they understood the secret of immortality, they attempted to betray their patrons and were cursed with undeath. This curse has only made the Vampire Lords more bitter and cruel as they rule brutally over their fearful subjects.
backgroundFull:
The Vampiric Undead originate from the western reaches of the Empire. Their lands were divided into a handful of counties made up of small villages scattered over the Western Steppes, beyond the Dwarven Mountains. Far from the centre of the Old Empire, these lands were undeveloped and often overlooked, raided by nomadic Ogres and other neighbours. 

When the Havoc Wars began, most of the armies and nobility of the Steppes were summoned, along with the rest of the Imperial vassals, to defend the Empire’s northern borders. The Steppe was left largely unguarded, and it was soon overrun by marauding neighbours and outlaws. Desperate to defend their lands, the remaining nobles began to listen to the promises of an exiled wizard, known as the Great Necromancer. This wizard offered these nobles the armies that they needed, in exchange for an oath of loyalty to his mysterious patrons. Those nobles who accepted his offer would see their enemies driven out and their graveyards emptied, as the wizard raised the dead to fight. 

The Great Necromancer introduced the nobles to his patrons, strange and lifeless beings from another plane. These patrons offered the nobility the secret of immortality if the nobles would give them a piece of Tyria to live in. The nobles eagerly accepted the pact and began using their undead armies to conquer their neighbours to carve out a new realm. Yet, when the time came to complete the deal, they betrayed the wizard and his patrons, severing the link between the planes, and stealing the knowledge for themselves. 

They eagerly attempted the ritual, sacrificing the wizard in the process. However, the ritual did not result in their immortality, but instead turned them into the first generation of Tyrian Vampires. The Vampiric Nobles, lacking a clear leader, shifted the blame on each other for the ritual’s failure, and soon fought for dominance over the rest. These Vampires viewed their mortal subjects as mere cattle, useful only as nourishment and a means to create more undead. 

When the Rift opened, some whispered that the Great Necromancer’s old patrons had returned, seeking revenge. Meanwhile, from the east, one of the Emperor’s own children arrived in the steppes as an undead immortal. Desperate and weary of their endless internal conflicts, many Vampires have submitted to him, hoping that they might unite together to protect themselves and expand their realms once more. 

How will you harness your power over death itself?

product.description: Standing taller than any Human, a Werewolf Champion is a formidable opponent; their claws can pierce a breastplate, and they wield even sharper blades. These Champions harbour a ravenous hunger caused by the Curse that pushes them to track their prey relentlessly. It is as if the wildness of the deep forests of the Vampiric Marches had coalesced into one being of primitive fury. Werewolf Champions are pack leaders, those who were able to prove their strength and survive the Vremyasag while also retaining enough of their sanity to prevent the Curse from turning them into mindless beasts.

Vampire Lords are dangerous adversaries. Despite their Human-like appearance, they are infused with the wretched energy of the Curse, which confers them strength and vigour far beyond those of mere mortals, as well as innate arcane powers that some of them have used to master the dark art of necromancy. Doomed to forever suffer from an inextinguishable thirst for blood, Vampire Lords unleash their repressed urges on the battlefield, turning them into ferocious fighters that will stop at nothing to strike down their opponents.

Ghoul Champions are the smartest and strongest of their kin. Even grizzled veterans can find themselves shaking in fear when they see a snarling creature leap at them, its toxin claws dripping with venom, its wounds seemingly healing in mere minutes. Where most Ghouls are unable to express themselves beyond unnerving groans and yelps, Champions can somewhat communicate with other species. And while they look just as horrifying as their brethren, they can be deceivingly intelligent, on par with any elegant Vampire.

Among the indifferent ranks of Skeletons, who move at a uniform pace, bound by the spells that raised them, Skeleton Champions stand out. Beyond the stark blackness of their orbits, there seems to be a glimmer of individuality. When their skull suddenly turns to face a particular enemy, and they raise their weapon to issue a challenge, it is as shocking as seeing a puppet suddenly ignore its strings.

Few Vampiric Undead armies take to the field without at least one Necromancer; they are Humans who have learnt the secrets of the Curse and can use its energy to cast spells and raise the dead. Contrary to Vampires, they have not been physically changed by the Curse, except for being able to prolong their lives beyond their natural years. Lacking the Vampires’ raw power, Necromancers focus on supporting their army by using their arcane knowledge to reinforce units, either by granting them additional strength and quickness or by summoning reinforcements to replenish thinning ranks.

Gremyir had fought as a Human under Sevrig I during the Havoc Wars, leading his tribe of Volshoboz (Forest people) in ambushes and raids. He had become an expert in irregular warfare, and the Havoc Warriors had nicknamed him the Night Hunter. When the Curse turned him into a Werewolf, Gremyir naturally became the Champion of a pack composed of other former forest peoples. Lady Imruskoza, Marchioness of Telen Valley, was only fourteen years old when the Curse turned her into a Vampire. Her father and brothers had been slain at the battle of the Red Road and she had inherited the family title.

product.description: The love story between Navleva and her husband Count Grevrig is one of the great romances of the Marches; many songs have been written about their story, from its heartwarming start to its tragic ending. Navleva was born in a Human town close to Verdorv. The Count fell in love with her at first sight and so did she. After several years of marriage, she asked him to make her a Vampire so that they could spend eternity together. Like her husband, the Countess became a fervent proponent of undead-mortal cohabitation and maintained a large correspondence with several scholars.

Ekvanyik “Blackfang” Tsaveskoz, an infamous Vampire adventurer, started as the Knight-Commander of the port town of Grazye. Unsatisfied with his low place in the ranks of Vampire Nobility, Tsaveskoz sought to make a name for himself, and decided to find outside of the Marches the glory that he couldn’t attain in his homeland.  Before he even took the name Blackfang, Knight-Commander Tsaveskoz was known for his greed. He had been a fearsome warrior in his mortal days, ruthlessly cutting down Havoc Warriors with his cutlass.

Latmyir the Mad is a powerful necromancer obsessed with perfecting the art of raising Skeletons. He was one of the earliest apprentices of the Stranger. Some have said that the Curse drove him mad, while others insist he was exactly the same before. In order to capture more of the warrior’s souls, Latmyir conducts experiments with long burials accompanied with varied rituals. He keeps running into the problem that most of the souls he drags back into their skeletons react very poorly to it. His enemies are terrified by tales of him trapping his enemy’s souls into inanimate objects.

Even though they are far from elite units, these Archers enjoy a special status in their villages. Only those who have been chosen by their Lord are allowed the use of a bow, and they learn their craft by participating in hunts whenever required. Being an Archer is seen as having a special tie to the nobility, even if it does not come with any specific reward.

Units of Skeleton Guard form the backbone of most Vampiric Undead armies. Marching in unison, silent but for the sounds of footsteps and the rustling of bones, they embody the sinister might of the Marches, ready to fall and be raised again a thousand times in service of their immortal masters. Skeletons are not usually raised with a snap of the fingers; they are carefully crafted weapons of war. The spirits of fallen warriors are bound to their earthly remains by the expert spells of Necromancers, their emotions and individuality stripped away, leaving only the parts of them dedicated to war.

Bursting forth out of the shadows to lacerate their prey with their razor-sharp claws, Ghouls are the unsettling scouts of the Vampiric Undead. Driven half-mad by the Curse and experiments inflicted upon them by their Necromancer masters, they let their pent-up fury loose on the battlefield. As victims of the Curse sickness, their former Human bodies became distorted, turning into half-bat creatures, both in shape and behaviour. Their language is hard to decipher, and their behaviour is often puzzling, as the Curse afflicts them with random hallucinations and other pangs of madness.

Zombie Wolves haunt the woods and plains of the Vampiric Marches and run ahead of campaigning armies. Their flesh may be rotting, but their claws are sharp, and the hunger that possesses them makes them fiercer than their mortal kin, for it can never be satisfied. Wolves have always been present in the region of the Marches; they can be found on banners and decorations from generations ago, and nobles had a duty to hunt them to protect their subjects. The Curse has made wolves scarce, as their prey populations have dwindled.

It is said that a good marksman, to hit his target and steady his aim, needs to breathe out first before letting his arrow fly. Steady aim has never been an issue for the Skeleton Watch; their crossbows never shake, and their lack of eyes does not seem to prevent them from raining bolts down upon their enemies. The first role of the Skeleton Watch is to stand guard on castle walls and other high points. Their constant alertness makes them very efficient at that role, as the Ratmen who tried to infiltrate Zerkhyiv castle shortly after the Rift opened discovered.

Skeleton Knights ride to battle with a grim smile on their bleached skulls, carrying out the will of their Lord, ready to die in battle as many times as necessary. Their eerie silence and lack of expression make them extremely unnerving to face. Not all Knights are Champions; many of them do not have enough left of their personality to become leaders. While a Champion is able to conceive long-term plans and has some amount of personal ambition, most Skeleton Knights care for nothing beyond their next battle.

Vampire Knights are elite fighters, members of the aristocracy of the Marches clad in the best armour available and riding priceless undead steeds, whose powerful charges can dislocate the tightest defensive lines. When they ride into combat, their faces become distorted as they let the fury of the Curse wash over them. But their movements remain perfectly choreographed, guided by centuries of fighting experience. These units are often composed of low-ranking nobles who are either part of a Lord’s house or have agreed to lend their support to said Lord.

Drained Soldiers are members of the Vampiric Marches’ peasantry. Armed with a ramshackle mix of old weapons and agricultural equipment, they go into battle at their Lord’s behest, compensating for their lack of formal training with numbers and fanatical determination. Unlike most other creatures, they are not fully undead; their lifespan is artificially prolonged by the Dogozmenye, a yearly ritual during which their Lord focuses the energy of the Curse into them.

Shambling hordes of Stitched Zombies are a frequent sight in Vampiric Undead armies. Lurching forwards with awkward, twitchy movements, they are preceded by the stench of their rotting flesh. Meaningless groans emanate from their mouths as blank eyes roll around in their orbits. While a single Stitched is easy to dispatch, more always come, summoned by their Corpse Master, climbing over the still-moving bodies of their fallen peers. They are mindless, devoid of even the shred of identity that a Ghoul or Skeleton Guard still clings onto.

Bats are everywhere in the Vampiric Marches and are considered sacred animals. While they were already present before the Ritual, their numbers seem to have grown considerably since, in contrast to most other animal species. They seem to have a particular link to necromantic energy, whether that was an intended part of the Stranger’s Curse or simply due to their presence during the events at Kamzan Castle.

Towering above their Stitched brethren, Stitched Butchers are enormous, disgusting masses of sewn-together flesh armed with massive cleavers and rudimentary spiked prosthetics. Accompanied by the buzzing of flies, they stomp across the battlefield, chopping down valuable body parts and those who try to stop them. Corpse Masters use Stitched Butchers as both bodyguards and draft animals. These gigantic brutes carry large baskets on their backs, which they fill with any loose limb, torso, and head they can find.

Giant Bats are large enough to grab a man and drag him away. These beasts are feared by most and can sow chaos in enemy ranks; the bats burst from the shadows to furiously mangle their prey, driven by Curse-induced bloodthirst. The first Giant Bats were the result of Necromancers experimenting in their quest to understand the effects of the Curse, which seemed to impact Humans and bats in similar ways. Many of the bats were released into the wild, either intentionally or by devouring their creator, and they are now a part of the Vampiric Marches’ fauna.

Towering over their regular-sized cousins, Ghoul Horrors are hulking brutes that can mangle any experienced soldier with their sheer strength and ferocity. Deceptively agile for their size, they can leap out of the most unexpected places and make their target regret they dared to challenge the Vampiric Undead. Ghoul Horrors were initially created by Necromancers who needed servants able to carry heavy loads across the uneven terrain of the Marches.

The changes which most Vampires undergo as a result of the Transfusion ritual do not greatly change their physical form; their canines grow sharper, and sometimes their ears grow more pointed, but they remain recognisable. This is not always the case, however. Sometimes due to an issue with the ritual, severe Curse sickness, neglecting proper protection in the practice of necromancy, or just bad luck, their bodies may be subject to far more radical changes. Most of these unfortunate individuals are transformed into twisted, winged monsters known as Bat Horrors.

Werewolves are the ultimate hunters. Muscular, ferocious, and agile, they can sprint through a forest as if it were an open field and take down large beasts with their blades and claws. Facing off against a Werewolf pack deep in the woods is an experience that few have endured and lived to tell the tale. Even before the Ritual, the forest tribes, or Volshoboz, were expert woodsmen. The Curse may have infected them with a never-ending hunger, but it also improved their senses and their strength.

product.description: The sombre elegance and threatening aura of a Vampire Lord mounted on their Undead Steed are unmatched. Whether they are leading the charge, galloping between units to coordinate the ranks, or issuing a challenge to an enemy leader, Vampire Lords are the striking image of their country, a land of fierce warriors changed by a fateful curse. Necromancers create Steeds with the utmost care, as they are considered an extension of their rider. Thanks to their Undead nature, they never tire nor need to feed, except for the occasional piece of flesh found on the battlefield.

The thunderous gallop of a mounted Vampire approaching is a sound that sends chills down the spine of their enemies. But the most experienced know that the most worrying part is when that sound suddenly stops, for it means that they need to stop looking ahead and start looking up into the dark sky.
For millennia, riding a horse has been one of the symbols of the high status enjoyed by the nobles of the Marches. After the Ritual transformed the country and made it difficult to breed quality horses, significant expenses were incurred to develop an Undead steed that could properly serve.

gains.name: Winged Terror

product.description: When a Vampire Lord descends from the sky on a Winged Terror, the wise run for cover. These massive beasts can rip a horse’s head clean off and are prone to Curse-induced pangs of hunger that can lead them to swallow a Human whole, while the Vampire rider is a consummate fighter who can control their mount as if it were an extension of themselves. It goes without saying that a Winged Terror is a fear-inducing sight. These Undead monsters are the mounts of choice of Vampire Lords when they want to lead devastating charges on powerful enemy units.

product.description: When mounted on a powerful Undead Steed, a Skeleton Champion becomes a figure of impending doom, appearing as a herald of death to lead legions of the fallen into battle. They are often nobles of the old Western Marches, who died long before the Ritual and were raised afterwards, drawn from their ceremonial tumuli or crypts to fight once again. It is not uncommon for a Vampire to have several Skeleton Champions in his armies that are his own ancestors.

product.description: Corpse Masters walk to battle wearing raggedy clothes and carrying a gallows-shaped staff from which hang rotting body parts, the material that gave them their name. Wild Curse energy emanates from them, seeming to darken the air around them. With a flick of the wrist, they are able to control the movements of dozens of Stitched Zombies, sending them shambling towards the enemy like grotesque flesh puppets.

Chosen from among the most promising Champions, Skeleton Commanders represent the epitome of their kind. They possess all of the cunning and martial skill they once had in life, combined with the resolute loyalty and unwavering determination imbued by the Necromancer who raised them. Skeleton Commanders are relentless in pursuit of their goals and extremely difficult to truly kill, making them a force to be reckoned with.

specialRules.name: Repel Ambushers
specialRules.description: Enemy units using Ambush must be set up over 12" away from this model's unit.

specialRules.name: Instinctive
specialRules.description: When this model is activated, if it is able to shoot/charge an enemy unit, then it must immediately attack the closest valid target and gets +1 to hit rolls for that attack.

specialRules.name: Infiltrate
specialRules.description: Counts as having Ambush, but may be deployed anywhere over 3" away from enemy unit.

specialRules.name: No Retreat Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get No Retreat. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Stealth Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Stealth. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Teleport
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, you may place this model anywhere fully within 3" of its position when using Advance/Charge actions, or fully within 6" of its position when using Rush actions.

specialRules.name: Sergeant
specialRules.description: This model gets AP(+1) when attacking.

specialRules.name: Fast Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game moves +2" when using Advance actions and +4" when using Rush/Charge actions. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Unique Hero
specialRules.description: Counts as having Hero, and this model may only be taken once per army.

specialRules.name: Ambush Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Ambush. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Reanimation Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Reanimation. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Bane when Shooting
specialRules.description: This model gets Bane when shooting.

specialRules.name: Ravage
specialRules.description: Once per round, when it’s this model’s turn to strike in melee, roll X dice before attacking, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 6+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Cursed Undead
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Shred in Melee Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Shred in melee. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Scout Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Scout. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Cursed Undead
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Cursed Undead, they ignore wounds on rolls of 5-6 from Cursed Undead (instead of only on 6+).

specialRules.name: Enhanced Cursed Undead Buff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 friendly units within 12", which gets Enhanced Cursed Undead once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Brace in Melee
specialRules.description: This model gets Brace(1) in melee.

specialRules.name: Fragment
specialRules.description: When attacking units where most models have Defense 4+ to Defense 6+, the target must re-roll successful unmodified Defense results of 4-6.

specialRules.name: Piercing Marksman Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 friendly units picked before the start of the game get Piercing Marksman. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Mind Control
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which must take a Morale Test. If failed you may move it by up to 6" in a straight line in any direction. Units may only be moved once per round in this way.

specialRules.name: Protected
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Protected
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Protected, they ignore wounds on rolls of 5-6 from Protected (instead of only on 6+).

specialRules.name: Ambush
specialRules.description: May be set aside before deployment. At the start of any round after the first, may be deployed anywhere over 9” away from enemy units. Players alternate in placing Ambush units, starting with the player that activates next. Units that deploy via Ambush can’t seize or contest objectives on the round they deploy.

specialRules.name: No Retreat
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule fails a Morale Test that causes it to be Shaken or Routed, the test counts as passed instead. Then, roll as many dice as the number of wounds it would take to fully destroy it, and for each result of 1-3 the unit takes one wound, which can't be ignored.

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: When units where most models have this rule are shot from over 9" away, enemy units get -1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: Units within 6” of friendly Heroes may use the Hero’s Quality for Morale Tests as long as the Hero isn’t Shaken.

specialRules.name: Reanimation
specialRules.description: When a unit where all models have this rule is activated, roll as many dice as the max. number of models/wounds it could restore. For each 5+ you may restore one model/wound. Note that new models may only be restored if they can be placed in coherency with non-restored models.

specialRules.name: Bane
specialRules.description: Ignores Regeneration, and when attacking, the target must re-roll unmodified Defense results of 6.

specialRules.name: Shred
specialRules.description: For each unmodified result of 1 to block hits, this weapon deals 1 extra wound.

specialRules.name: Scout
specialRules.description: May be set aside before deployment. After all other units are deployed, may be deployed anywhere fully within 9” of their deployment zone, over 9” away from non-Scout enemy units. Players alternate in placing Scout units, starting with the player that activates next.

specialRules.name: Brace
specialRules.description: Enemies charging this unit get -X total Impact rolls, unless this unit is Fatigued.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Piercing Marksman
specialRules.description: When shooting at enemies over 9" away, this model's weapons get AP(+1).

specialRules.name: Deadly
specialRules.description: Assign each wound to one model, and multiply it by X. Hits from Deadly must be resolved first, and these wounds don’t carry over to other models if the original target is killed.
